title: Summary lift-plan Review records its session under core-engine, not the reviewed module
body:
## Summary
The Summary's lift-plan Review dispatches every module's feature-review through one useModuleCLI bound to moduleId 'core-engine', so the session outcome, terminal tab and anti-pattern check are attributed to core-engine.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/UnifiedSummaryView/useUnifiedSummaryView.ts:147 binds useModuleCLI to `'core-engine' as SubModuleId`; actOnLift (same file, review branch) dispatches TaskFactory.featureReview(action.moduleId, ...) for any module. src/hooks/useModuleCLI.ts:119 records recordSessionOutcome with moduleIdRef.current (core-engine) and src/hooks/useModuleCLI.ts:166 runs checkPromptBeforeDispatch against opts.moduleId. The Summary's own Activity dimension is computed from per-module session analytics, so reviewing arpg-loot credits core-engine's activity and leaves loot's untouched: the remedy cannot move the number it was priced against. Fixed: useModuleCLI.execute accepts a per-dispatch moduleId override (or the Summary keys one CLI door per module), and the recorded outcome names the reviewed module.

## Flow
- open Evaluator > Summary, select a module cell (e.g. arpg-loot), click Review
- useModuleCLI records the outcome with moduleId core-engine
- session analytics: core-engine +1 session, arpg-loot +0; loot's Activity dimension does not move

## Expected impact
Operators acting on a lift see the lifted module's Activity change; per-module analytics become truthful. Could break: the shared useModuleCLI signature (an additive override keeps every caller unchanged).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the remedy's session is attributed to the module it reviewed
Before: 1 of 1 Review dispatch paths records moduleId core-engine regardless of the reviewed module (read: useUnifiedSummaryView.ts:147 + useModuleCLI.ts:119)
After: predicted 0 of 1 - the recorded moduleId equals action.moduleId
Method: simulation - walked arpg-loot / arpg-combat / animations reviews through actOnLift -> useModuleCLI; the fix and its test sit in the shared hook, outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/components/modules/evaluator/UnifiedSummaryView/useUnifiedSummaryView.ts:147  moduleId: 'core-engine' as SubModuleId,
src/hooks/useModuleCLI.ts:119  moduleId: moduleIdRef.current,
src/hooks/useModuleCLI.ts:166  .checkPromptBeforeDispatch(prompt, opts.moduleId)
instrument: a test that mocks recordSessionOutcome, clicks Review on the arpg-loot lift plan and asserts the recorded moduleId is arpg-loot (red today: core-engine)

title: Session Analytics quick-nav reads 'No data' when the analytics read failed
body:
## Summary
When /api/session-analytics fails on first load, the Session Analytics quick-nav card and the A source badge both say 'No data', the same words as a project with zero sessions.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/UnifiedSummaryView/index.tsx:260 renders `analytics ? ... : 'No data'`; src/components/modules/evaluator/UnifiedSummaryView/useUnifiedSummaryView.ts:171 sets sourceStatus.analytics false for a null analytics, and src/components/modules/evaluator/UnifiedSummaryView/SourceBadge.tsx:21 titles it 'No data'. The error banner above names the failure, but the two per-source surfaces still claim emptiness - the hollow-clean shape. Fixed: the hook exposes per-source error, and the card and badge read 'Load failed' (a distinct badge state) for a source whose read failed.

## Flow
- analytics endpoint returns HTTP 500 on mount
- analyticsError set, analytics null
- QuickNavCard sub = 'No data', badge A title = 'A: No data'

## Expected impact
The per-source surfaces stop contradicting the banner. Could break: nothing beyond the two labels.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a failed source is labelled failed, not empty
Before: 2 surfaces (quick-nav sub, source badge) read 'No data' for a failed analytics read (walked)
After: predicted 0 of 2
Method: simulation - walked the HTTP 500 path through the hook and both components; no test yet
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: component test: tryApiFetch resolves {ok:false,error:'HTTP 500'} on mount; assert the Session Analytics card does not read 'No data' (red today)

title: Summary source badges convey availability by colour and title only
body:
## Summary
The four Q/D/A/S source badges expose availability only through icon colour and a title tooltip; they have no accessible name or state.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/UnifiedSummaryView/SourceBadge.tsx:15 renders a plain div with a title, and src/components/modules/evaluator/UnifiedSummaryView/SourceBadge.tsx:25 flips the icon colour between var(--text) and var(--text-subtle); no role, aria-label or text. A title is not reliably announced (WCAG 1.4.1 use of colour, 4.1.2 name/role/value); the 'n/4 sources' count is the only text. Fixed: each badge gets an accessible name ('Quality: data available') and a non-colour cue per the repo's StatusToken convention.

## Flow
- screen reader moves through the Summary header
- the four badges announce nothing
- a colour-blind user sees two near-identical greys

## Expected impact
Assistive-tech users learn which sources fed the composite. Could break: nothing; additive attributes.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - each source badge has an accessible name stating its availability
Before: 0 of 4 badges carry an accessible name (read)
After: predicted 4 of 4
Method: simulation - read the component; the non-colour cue is a small design choice, so not built unattended
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: render test counting badges with a non-empty accessible name (aria-label or role=img name): 0/4 today

title: Project Health CSS charts expose no text alternative
body:
## Summary
The SVG charts on the Velocity/Quality/Milestones tabs (LineChartSimple, AreaChartSimple, BurndownChart) and the div-based BarChartSimple have no role or accessible summary.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/HolisticHealthView/charts.tsx:44, src/components/modules/evaluator/HolisticHealthView/charts.tsx:83 and src/components/modules/evaluator/HolisticHealthView/charts.tsx:121 render bare <svg> elements with no role, aria-label or <title>; BarChartSimple (src/components/modules/evaluator/HolisticHealthView/charts.tsx:5) is divs with numbers and no list or table semantics. A screen-reader user gets a run of loose labels. Fixed: role=img with an aria-label summarising the series (first/last value, trend), or a visually hidden data table, per the data-viz golden path.

## Flow
- open Project Health > Quality
- the trend chart is announced as nothing (svg without a name)
- only the x-axis labels are read, detached from their values

## Expected impact
The trend and burndown become perceivable without sight. Could break: nothing visual.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - every chart has a text alternative
Before: 0 of 4 charts carry an accessible name (read)
After: predicted 4 of 4
Method: simulation - read the four components; one summary per chart shape makes this M
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: render test per chart asserting an element with role=img and a non-empty aria-label naming the last value: 0/4 today

title: Quality trend gridlines do not correspond to the plotted scale
body:
## Summary
LineChartSimple draws gridlines at fixed 0/25/50/75/100% of the chart height while it plots points on a min..max-normalised scale with an 8px inset, so the lines mark no value.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/HolisticHealthView/charts.tsx:36 and src/components/modules/evaluator/HolisticHealthView/charts.tsx:40 place gridlines at `h - (pct/100)*h`; points use `h - ((v-min)/range)*(h-16) - 8` with min = min(values, 0) and max = max(values, 1) (src/components/modules/evaluator/HolisticHealthView/charts.tsx:28). There are no axis labels, so the grid reads as a 0-100 scale it is not. Fixed: for a 0-100 score series pin the domain to 0..100 and label the lines, or drop the grid.

## Flow
- two scans scoring 55 and 60
- the 100% gridline sits at score 60
- a reader takes the top line as 100 and reads the latest scan as ~100

## Expected impact
The trend stops overstating the latest score. Could break: chart appearance (intended).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the gridlines mean a value
Before: for data [55,60]: min 0, max 60, so the top (100%) gridline marks 60, not 100 (computed by hand)
After: predicted: with a fixed 0..100 domain the top gridline marks 100
Method: simulation - computed the mapping for [55,60]; a geometry test is S
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: geometry test: render LineChartSimple with [55,60]; assert the point for 60 is not on the top gridline (red today)

title: Velocity/Quality/Milestones tabs render headed empty cards when history is empty
body:
## Summary
With no scans or dated completions the charts return null and the tabs show card headings over blank space instead of an empty-state line.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/HolisticHealthView/charts.tsx:27, src/components/modules/evaluator/HolisticHealthView/charts.tsx:76 and src/components/modules/evaluator/HolisticHealthView/charts.tsx:114 return null on an empty series; QualityTab's Issues Trend list and MilestonesTab map empty arrays. Each card keeps its heading ('Quality Score Trend', 'Burndown Chart') above nothing, indistinguishable from a render failure. Fixed: each chart card renders a one-line empty state naming what populates it (run a scan; complete a dated checklist item).

## Flow
- fresh project, open Project Health > Quality
- 'Quality Score Trend' and 'Issues Trend' headings over empty cards

## Expected impact
First-run users learn what fills each chart. Could break: nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - an empty series says so
Before: 5 chart/list cards across 3 tabs render a heading over nothing on empty input (walked)
After: predicted 0 of 5
Method: simulation - walked each tab with empty arrays; a render test is S
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: render each tab with empty histories; assert each card has non-heading text (0/5 today)

title: Module Health stat card is blank and unlabelled when no module is scored
body:
## Summary
The Project Health 'Module Health' stat renders only non-zero badges, so an all-not-started project shows an empty row; the badges themselves are bare numbers told apart by colour.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/HolisticHealthView/index.tsx:204 and src/components/modules/evaluator/HolisticHealthView/index.tsx:206 render `healthyModules > 0 && <Badge variant="success">n</Badge>` (and warning/critical); not-started modules are never counted. With every module not-started the card is a label over nothing; with values, '3 2 1' carries meaning by hue only (WCAG 1.4.1). Fixed: label each count ('3 healthy') and render 'none scored (N not started)' when all are zero.

## Flow
- fresh project, open Project Health
- Module Health card shows its label and an empty badge row

## Expected impact
The stat card always says something true. Could break: card width.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the card states its counts in words
Before: 0 of 3 badges carry a word; the all-zero case renders no text under the label (read)
After: predicted 3 of 3 labelled; the all-zero case renders a sentence
Method: simulation - read the JSX; a render test is S
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: render with moduleHealth all not-started; assert the Module Health card has text beyond its label (red today)

title: Summary and Project Health tablists lack arrow-key navigation and tabpanel wiring
body:
## Summary
ViewModeToggle (and the Project Health SubTab tablist given roles this round) declare role=tablist/tab but implement neither roving tabindex/arrow keys nor aria-controls to a role=tabpanel.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/UnifiedSummaryView/ViewModeToggle.tsx:17 role=tablist and src/components/modules/evaluator/UnifiedSummaryView/ViewModeToggle.tsx:55 role=tab with aria-selected; no onKeyDown, every tab stays in the tab order, and the content is not a tabpanel. The ARIA tabs pattern announces a contract the widget does not keep; the Evaluator module's own TabButton already implements onArrowNav (src/components/modules/evaluator/EvaluatorModule/index.tsx:91). Fixed: roving tabindex + Left/Right and aria-controls/tabpanel ids for both tablists.

## Flow
- keyboard user tabs to 'Detailed', presses Right
- nothing happens; Tab moves to 'Brief' instead

## Expected impact
Keyboard users get the tab behaviour the role promises. Could break: focus order (intended).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - declared tabs behave as tabs
Before: 0 of 2 tablists in the context handle arrow keys; 0 tabpanels (read)
After: predicted 2 of 2
Method: simulation - read both components and the EvaluatorModule TabButton reference; a keyboard test is S each
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: fireEvent.keyDown ArrowRight on the selected tab; assert selection/focus moves (red today for both tablists)

title: Project Health shows a stale summary under a refresh error with no staleness cue
body:
## Summary
When a recompute fails after a prior success, the error card renders above the old summary and every stat reads as current.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/HolisticHealthView/index.tsx:72 renders the error card, and the `summary &&` block below keeps rendering the previous summary; src/stores/projectHealthStore.ts:97 sets only error/isLoading on failure, keeping summary. Nothing on the stats says they predate the failed recompute. Fixed: while error is set, mark the stats row 'from the last successful compute (time)' or dim it.

## Flow
- load Project Health successfully
- tick a checklist item; the recompute POST fails
- error card shows; completion % still shows the pre-tick value with no marker

## Expected impact
Readers stop trusting numbers that are behind. Could break: nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - stale numbers are labelled stale
Before: 0 staleness cues when error && summary (read)
After: predicted 1 cue on the stats row
Method: simulation - walked the store's failure path; a render test is S
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/components/modules/evaluator/HolisticHealthView/index.tsx:72  {error && (
src/stores/projectHealthStore.ts:97  set({ error: ..., isLoading: false })  // summary kept
instrument: render with error set and a summary present; assert a staleness marker is present (red today)
